source.title: Critical Influence of Overparameterization on Sharpness-aware Minimization
source.authors: Sungbin Shin; Dongyeop Lee; Maksym Andriushchenko; Namhoon Lee

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation affecting the reported result.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether increasing network width lowers test error, using a synthetic regression experiment with SAM rather than the version’s specified MNIST/CIFAR one-hidden-layer ReLU setup.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports validation-metric improvements from SAM across model scales and workloads, but those results measure SAM’s improvement over baseline optimizers, not the test-error-versus-width result named in V2. Figure-only details are not reconstructed as numbers.
record.test_reason: Appendix I directly measures held-out error as network width increases, extending V2's width–generalization question to synthetic regression trained with SAM. It does not establish that the tested widths are beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete: the authors find that SAM's relative generalization benefit generally increases with overparameterization, with sufficient regularization required. Separately, Appendix I reports decreasing synthetic-regression test error with width and provides a conditional population-loss guarantee.
record.recipe_differences: The test-error sweep uses SAM on synthetic regression with a two-layer ReLU network, training only first-layer weights. The version specifies one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that SAM’s benefit from overparameterization depends on regularization: the benefit does not always increase without weight decay, early stopping, or sufficient inductive bias. This qualification is for its broader SAM-versus-baseline validation results, not a separate test-error result in R1.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM's validation-performance advantage over its baseline optimizer generally increases with model size, subject to sufficient regularization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overparameterization can increase the relative generalization benefit of SAM.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM reaches minima with lower Hessian sharpness and more uniform Hessian moments than SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM imposes stronger local stability constraints on attained minima than SGD.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence (UAI), 2023
record.problems: The test-error sweep is shown only in a figure, with no textual numerical values or uncertainty reported. It uses a synthetic dataset and a SAM training recipe, so it does not directly establish the specified MNIST/CIFAR result.
record.rows_left_out: Section 3 and Appendix B report validation-metric comparisons between SAM and baseline optimizers over model scales and workloads. These are not rows for V2 because they report SAM’s improvement over a baseline rather than the test-error-versus-width outcome named by that version. Other figure-only results about sharpness, Hessian moments, and convergence do not measure a listed version.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy.

Whether error continues decreasing specifically beyond the width required for zero training error; training to convergence without explicit regularization using standard gradient training on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers under comparable tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance ranking generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: The generalization theorem complements R1: sufficiently wide networks achieve expected population loss at most OPT plus epsilon under prescribed initialization, sample-size and training-parameter conditions. It is an attainable-loss guarantee, not proof that realized test error decreases monotonically with width under a fixed recipe.
missing.locator: Appendix I, Theorem I.1; Appendix J, Theorem J.1

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text supports the selected excerpt despite its extraction-verification warning. SAM's relative advantage and Hessian measurements do not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap ranking. Missing interpolation evidence is an untested condition, not an observed failure of V2.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
The specified one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10; the paper’s test-error experiment is synthetic regression using a two-layer MLP and SAM.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons under the version’s tuning conditions.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
The effect of adding dropout on held-out error.
Whether magnitude-aware sharpness ranks generalization gaps across networks.
The effect of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.

rows.subject: 2-layer ReLU networks
rows.operation_detail: Increased hidden-neuron count and measured test error in synthetic regression; only first-layer weights were trained.
rows.locator: Appendix I, Figure 21 and accompanying experiment description
rows.note: The text states that test error keeps decreasing with a larger number of neurons. The figure’s precise values are not transcribed.
rows.check: The decreasing test-error trend is explicitly stated in Figure 21's caption. Widths are 100, 500, 1000, 5000, 10000 and 50000 hidden neurons. Only first-layer weights are trained; biases and output weights remain frozen. Learning rate and SAM perturbation radius are grid-searched. Training errors and convergence checks are not reported, so this row establishes the width trend without identifying a post-interpolation regime.

relationships.condition: Synthetic regression with one-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained using SAM, with frozen biases and output weights.
relationships.reason: R1 reports decreasing test error with increasing width; this supports the width trend, while the post-interpolation and convergence conditions remain untested.
relationships.display_finding: The reported width benefit remains unverified, with interpolation and convergence also unestablished.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
